objectives.0: Identify region, variety, vintage and quality level
objectives.1: Understand the distinctive elements of German labels
slides.0.title: How to Read a German Wine Label
slides.0.subtitle: All the Secrets a Single Label Holds
slides.1.title: 🏷️ Essential Elements of a German Label
slides.1.items.0.text: Region (Anbaugebiet): one of the 13, e.g. Mosel, Pfalz, Rheingau
slides.1.items.3.text: Prädikat level: Kabinett / Spätlese / Auslese, etc.
slides.1.items.5.text: Vineyard name (Einzellage or Grosslage): e.g. Bernkasteler Doctor
slides.2.title: 📖 Key German Terms Explained
slides.2.content:
• Erzeugerabfüllung / Gutsabfüllung: estate-bottled (a quality guarantee)
• Einzellage: single vineyard (the most precise origin)
• Grosslage: a collective area of multiple vineyards (less precise)
• Trocken: dry (residual sugar < 9 g/L)
• Halbtrocken / Feinherb: off-dry
• Weißwein: white wine    Rotwein: red wine
• Sekt: sparkling wine
slides.3.title: Quick Quiz
slides.3.questions.0.question: What does 'Trocken' on a German label mean?
slides.3.questions.0.explanation: Trocken means 'dry' in German, indicating a low residual sugar wine (typically below 9 g/L) — a dry style.
slides.3.questions.1.question: What does 'Einzellage' mean?
slides.3.questions.1.explanation: Einzellage (plural Einzellagen) means 'single vineyard parcel' in German — the most precise origin designation in Germany, similar to a French Premier Cru.
